hypothesis: If whorl breadths of ammonoid shells form a geometric progression, then within individual specimens the whorl expansion rate (WER) measured at successive intervals along the growth spiral is approximately constant, so log(whorl size) is linear in whorl number.
pass_criterion: Using the Dryad Supplementary_data.xlsx, for specimens with at least 4 consecutive WER measurements on the median plane, the median within-specimen coefficient of variation of WER is at most 0.15, and at least 70% of specimens have a within-specimen WER range (max/min) of at most 1.3 across the measured growth stages after excluding the earliest ontogenetic stage (ammonitella and first whorl).
fail_criterion: The median within-specimen CV of WER exceeds 0.25, or fewer than 50% of specimens have a within-specimen WER max/min of at most 1.3 across measured growth stages after excluding the earliest stage. That would show non-constant expansion, so the whorl sizes are not a geometric progression.
interpretation: Thompson's "breadths of successive whorls along a radius" is a radial whorl size, which is not recorded directly here. A geometric progression of whorl breadth with a constant ratio is the same as a constant whorl expansion rate, which is Raup's W (the ratio of successive whorl size per revolution). The WER in this dataset is a modern proxy for that ratio. Modern reinterpretation: ammonoids show ontogenetic change in WER, especially in early growth, so the test excludes the earliest stage and allows the tolerance stated above. The dataset covers only Cretaceous ammonoids (Perisphinctina, Ancyloceratina). It has no Nautilus data and no gastropods, so it tests only the ammonitoid part of the claim. It cannot test the Nautilus "about three times as broad" ratio or the generalisation to gastropods, and a pass here would not establish those parts. The fields to be used are the specimen ID, taxon, and WER by growth stage (diameter). The column names have not been checked in the spreadsheet itself.

dataset.name: Measurement data for septal spacing and conch morphology in Cretaceous ammonoids
dataset.publisher: Dryad (data by Nishino, Komazaki, Arai, Hattori, Uoya, Iida and Wani, Yokohama National University)
dataset.why_it_fits: It gives the whorl expansion rate measured on the median plane at successive growth intervals for many Cretaceous ammonoid specimens, as Supplementary_data.xlsx (334 KB) with a README. Constancy of WER within a specimen is the modern equivalent of a geometric progression of whorl size. It covers ammonoids only, not Nautilus or gastropods.
